review.notes: Triage review of all 118 physical pages: automated normalized 4-gram page containment plus missing-run extraction against the OCR markdown (all pages machine-scanned), line-level inspection of every low-containment page, and 300-dpi renders for each patch. Full-code-fence scan balanced (one fence, the Table 26 prompt example). Flagged table pages (per-language result tables, xP3x/template lists, example generations) were verified present as HTML tables by spot checks; PDF cell-by-cell extraction order accounts for their low containment. "Answer (B): [COMPLETION A]" in Appendix D, "helpful following assistant" and the duplicated Bibliography/References headings all match the print. Punctuation spacing after inline math is handled by the shared OCR normalizer.

unresolved.evidence: xP3x/translated-dataset template tables occupy full pages; PDF text extraction reads cell-by-cell so automated diff cannot line-verify every row. Spot checks (adversarial_qa dbidaf, MultiEURLEX, Jeopardy with Context, None_ template names) all matched the HTML tables in the OCR markdown.

Table 28 contains degenerate model completions (e.g. repeated "AJAJAJA" runs, "sin" repeated characters) transcribed into the OCR table; consistent with the paper’s discussion of degenerate enumeration outputs but the full table was not visually verified cell-by-cell against the render.

Example generations in Sinhala/Arabic/etc. use complex scripts whose PDF text layer extracts with combining-mark oddities; n-gram containment is unreliable for these cells and they were not line-verified.
